scope: local optional process input bound and retained reserve bundle transport compatibility using supplied synthetic reports; no host or runtime admission

validation.skipScope: Existing Linux-only check on the local non-Linux host

inputContract.validation: Exact positive integer no greater than 32 MiB, checked before process creation even when input is absent. Input must remain immutable bytes within the selected limit.
inputContract.existingPreparer: Unchanged calls retain the 16 MiB default. No automatic increase or reserve invocation.
inputContract.outputAndTimeouts: Existing independent output limits, lifetime deadline, simultaneous pipe draining and owned process cleanup remain in force.

limitations: The six real bundle invocations use the existing deterministic two-account fixture, padded with valid JSON whitespace to 16 MiB plus one and exactly 32 MiB. They verify transport and unchanged output, not a maximum-account dataset or memory-performance benchmark.

Four refusal controls intercept process creation and confirm that the default 16 MiB limit and explicit 32 MiB maximum reject overflow before invocation. Real exact-size binary stdin delivery is separately covered by the Python tests.

Both adapter modes run with an explicit empty environment and 1 MiB stdout, 64 KiB stderr and 30-second lifetime limits. All permission flags and output values match the unpadded fixture. Inputs are not written to tool logs.

The selected Node executable and retained bundle hashes match before and after these local controls. This observation does not admit either artifact for a Linux deployment, constrain builtin capabilities or provide a sandbox.

The preparer still needs reviewed runtime selection, environment policy, reserve integration, fresh real compilation and strict replay. Existing genesis snapshot bounds and host admission checks are unchanged.
